replies.text: Ha, interference ni mudah je faham. Ia berlaku bila dua gelombang koheren (frekuensi sama, fasa tetap) bertemu dan bertindih, kita panggil prinsip superposisi. Bila puncak bertemu puncak atau lembah bertemu lembah, gelombang tu jadi kuat, ni lah interferens membina (constructive interference). Tapi bila puncak bertemu lembah, diorang cancel antara satu sama lain, jadi lemah atau hilang terus, tu pulak interferens membinasa (destructive interference).

AceZCzCckqc.question: Sir, can you please answer in English because I am in DLP class. If I stand in front of a concave mirror and slowly walk towards it, at one point my face becomes inverted, but when I get very close to the mirror, my face suddenly becomes upright and enlarged. Why does my face “flip” upside down and then flip back up again? 😂

replies.text:
Haha, this is classic concave mirror behaviour lah, and u just discovered it live with your own face! When u stand far away, u are beyond the centre of curvature C, so the mirror forms a real, inverted and diminished image. As u walk closer but still beyond the focal point F, the image stays real and inverted, that is why your face looks upside down. The moment u cross the principal focus F, something dramatic happens, the image position jumps to infinity, so at exactly F u see no clear image at all, just blur!

Then when u get very close, between F and the pole P, the mirror switches to forming a virtual, upright and magnified image behind the mirror, so suddenly your face flips back up and looks big, kan? So it is not magic lah, u simply crossed the focal point, and that is the exact boundary where a concave mirror changes from real inverted image to virtual upright image. Try it slowly one more time and watch the flip happen right at F, very satisfying! 😄
